question: The majority of acute rhinosinusitis episodes are viral in origin and do not require antibiotic treatment.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Most acute rhinosinusitis is viral (rhinovirus, influenza). Blanket antibiotic prescribing is a major driver of antimicrobial resistance. Reserve antibiotics for genuine bacterial sinusitis with specific diagnostic criteria.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Approximately 90–98% of acute rhinosinusitis is viral. Antibiotics are indicated only when bacterial infection is confirmed or strongly suspected — typically when symptoms worsen after 5 days or persist beyond 10 days, or when severe symptoms (high fever, unilateral facial pain, purulent unilateral discharge) are present.
